hooks.text: Most people assume a stellar collapse creates an instant cosmic vacuum cleaner.
If the Sun became a black hole, Earth would keep orbiting normally.
Would a black hole replacement swallow the entire solar system?

title: The Black Hole Vacuum Cleaner Myth
description: Discover what would actually happen if our Sun became a black hole. It turns out gravity doesn't work like a vacuum cleaner.

beats.text: Most people assume a stellar collapse creates an instant cosmic vacuum cleaner.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope image of a supernova remnant, 2005

beats.text: A black hole is indeed so dense that not even light can escape its gravitational grip.
beats.visual: artist concept of a black hole with an accretion disk

beats.text: The boundary of no escape is the event horizon, but its reach is surprisingly limited.
beats.visual: Event Horizon Telescope image of the M87 black hole, 2019
queries: M87 black hole Event Horizon Telescope

beats.text: From a distance, the gravitational field of a black hole is identical to any other body of the same mass.
beats.visual: diagram of spacetime curvature around a massive body

beats.text: If you replaced the Sun with a black hole of equal mass, the physics of gravity wouldn't change.
beats.visual: NASA illustration of Earth orbiting the Sun
queries: Earth orbit around Sun illustration NASA

beats.text: While the solar system would grow dark and freezing, the actual path of our planet wouldn't move an inch.
beats.visual: artist concept of a frozen Earth in a dark solar system
queries: Frozen Earth in space artist concept

beats.text: Our planets would stay in their current orbits instead of getting sucked inside.
beats.visual: NASA diagram of the solar system planets in their familiar paths

better_than_last: This episode applies the proven rule to deliver the core narrative setup immediately after the hook and structures the reveal around physical gravitational mechanics.
